_doc: The bundled font inventory: what each file is, where it came from, and what it must still be.
Scripts/fonts.py reads this. `check` hashes every entry and compares; `update`
re-fetches from `source` at `version` and rewrites the file. The hash is the
point: a font is a binary nobody reads in review, so a swapped or truncated
one passes every human check and changes every golden.
`axes` is not decoration. A face bundled to exercise a variation setting is
useless the moment it is replaced by a static build, and the replacement
renders fine — the settings simply stop doing anything, and the snapshots
that were supposed to pin them keep passing. Recording the axes here makes
that substitution a gate failure rather than a silent loss of coverage.
`licence_file` must exist beside the font. Bundling redistributes it, and the
OFL requires the licence to travel with the software.
ADDING A FILE HERE IS A RENDERING CHANGE UNTIL MEASURED OTHERWISE, even when
nothing selects it by name. macOS bundles this directory whole and registers it
through Info.plist's ATSApplicationFontsPath, so CoreText resolves a family from
whatever sits here — and given two files claiming one family it need not prefer
the one that was already shipping.
Worked example: two variable builds were added BESIDE the six static
instances of the same family, and the commit said it changed no rendering on any
arm because nothing selected them. CoreText resolved JetBrains Mono to the
variable file for regular and bold from the moment it landed. A bundle carrying
only the statics reads 118 pass / 1 fail; the same tree with the variable files
present reads 99 / 20. Eighteen of those twenty were sub-threshold — identical
ink counts and run positions, only channel values below the repaint cut — which
is why it read as noise for three weeks.
So attribute by RENDERING the bundle with and without the new file, not by
reading the diff: the diff shows an added file and no edit to any selector, which
is exactly what the failing case looks like. `CTFontCopyAttribute(font,
kCTFontURLAttribute)` reports which file actually won.
`member` may sit on each entry of `files` rather than on the font, for a release
archive that carries several of one family's files; the font-level `member` still
names the first file's when there is only one.
`url` names the whole download for a font whose upstream publishes no release
asset, and takes precedence over `source`/`version`/`asset` in `update`.

fonts.name: JetBrains Mono
fonts.role: The shipped primary face: what a terminal draws with when the user names no family. One file per slant, weight on the axis.
notes: Pinned to a COMMIT, not a tag or a branch, for the reason fetch-quic-deps.sh gives about the QUIC sources: a mutable ref means whoever can move it upstream chooses what ships.
Taken from master rather than a release. The last release, v2.304, is from January 2023; master carries 2.305 and two further years of fixes, so the released artefact is the older one here.

wght is 100-800 and defaults to 400. Measured against the v2.304 statics these replaced: the Regular instance is identical (stem 9.00, M advance 19.200), so body text did not move, but the rest of the ramp is heavier upstream — Bold 14.20 against 12.60, Medium 11.60 against 9.90. Bold text is visibly heavier than it was and `font.bold_weight` picks another coordinate for anyone who wants the old colour.
Read fonts/variable/, not fonts/archives/variable/: the archive copy is a release snapshot and differs (304208 bytes against 300144).

Not ttfautohint'd, where the statics were (v1.8.4.7-5d5b in their version string). FreeType honours TT hinting and CoreText ignores it, so replacing them re-minted the Linux goldens at small sizes while macOS saw only the weight change.

The bracket in the filename is a glob character class to a shell and to fnmatch. Every reference to it has to be quoted; unquoted it matches nothing here and would silently start matching if a one-character sibling ever appeared.

fonts.name: Monaspace Neon Var
fonts.role: The variable face the weight and width settings are pinned against. Not a shipped default; nothing selects it unless a configuration names it.
notes: The plain build, not the Nerd Font rebuild: the bundled Symbols Nerd Font is a glyph-only fallback that covers icons for whichever primary is selected, so patching the primary would duplicate coverage the fallback already provides at ten times the size.

Its wght axis DEFAULTS TO 200, not 400 — an unset font.weight draws this face ExtraLight. That is the case a weight setting has to survive, which is what makes it the right subject rather than a wrong one.
Reports traitMonoSpace = false while every printable-ASCII advance is identical, so a caller trusting the flag rejects a face that is monospaced in fact.

fonts.name: Symbols Nerd Font Mono
fonts.role: Glyph-only fallback for the icon ranges a text face does not cover. Never contributes metrics.
fonts.licence: MIT AND OFL-1.1 AND CC-BY-4.0 AND Apache-2.0 AND Bitstream-Vera AND Unlicense
fonts.notes: Unmodified Nerd Fonts v3.3.0 binary, verified against the pinned upstream file. SymbolsNerdFont-CONSTITUENTS.txt contains the constituent notices and terms; SymbolsNerdFont-LICENSE.txt retains the Nerd Fonts integration license.

fonts.name: GNU Unifont
fonts.role: The embedded bitmap tier: the last-resort face, baked into C++ rather than shipped as a font file.
fonts.notes: Not a bundled .ttf: gen-unifont.py bakes the .hex into UnifontData.cpp, so `update` regenerates rather than downloads a font file.

fonts.name: Monaspace Neon
fonts.role: The static family the texture-healing cases are set in: one file per style, so a bundle that has it draws the healed letterforms on every arm, iOS included. The Nerd Font rebuild is not bundled; the bundled Symbols Nerd Font is the glyph fallback for whichever primary is selected.
notes: Statics rather than the variable build beside them, because the healing cases are pinned to the letterforms at one weight and a variable build heals more weakly at its default instance; the static Regular is what the plate was minted with.
Declares the family "Monaspace Neon", distinct from the variable file's "Monaspace Neon Var", so the two do not compete for one name.

fonts.name: Noto Sans
fonts.role: The proportional face the Linux arm draws OSC 66 runs with. Apple platforms keep the system face; Linux has no system face to keep, so this is the one it defines.
notes: The unhinted statics: the Linux rasteriser runs FreeType's own hinting policy, and a hinted build would carry instructions a second policy then argues with.
Two files, Regular and Bold, because a proportional run is drawn regular or bold and nothing else.

fonts.name: Noto Color Emoji
fonts.role: The colour emoji face the Linux arm draws with, and the one a configuration may select on Apple platforms in place of the system emoji. COLRv1 outlines, not bitmap strikes, so it scales to any cell.
notes: Fetched by `url`, not from a release asset: the noto-emoji releases are tags with no attached files.
v2.048 is the build Fedora ships as google-noto-color-emoji-fonts 20250623; this is the release after it.
